Hello,I’m Fareda Ahmed

I’m a self-taught designer. I design notebook covers, logos and presentations, often built around the books, films and research I love.

See the work @designsbyfareda

About

A graduate who found design through slides

I recently graduated from the Interdisciplinary English Studies program at the Faculty of Arts, Ain Shams University. I started designing PowerPoint presentations in college using Canva, and it quickly became something I genuinely enjoy. I recently launched my Instagram page to share my designs. It’s still small, but it’s a space where I get to be creative, express myself, and grow at my own pace.

Notebook covers

Sixteen notebook designs, each shown as a front and back mockup. Most are fan designs for book series, grouped into collections. Tap a cover to enlarge it.

One of my first designs

“Hi Nerds! Let’s Talk Books.”

Meet Malak, the effortlessly cool book lover behind your favorite BookTok content. Known for her bold opinions, killer style and a deep love for all things literary, Malak is here to turn every scroll into a new reading obsession. From flipping pages to making big moves in the creative world, Malak proves that passion for books can open real doors.

Rust orange and chocolate brown, with floating books around the character. The back cover keeps the palette and carries my signature, Designs by fareda. I made it together with the logo below.

University projects

Nine projects

One print ad and eight presentations, made for university courses. Each presentation opens in a new tab.

  1. 1
    2022Language & MeaningPrint ad

    “Do Nut Give Up”

    A print ad promoting peanuts as a workout snack. It combines linguistics and visual design, using an idiom, a metaphor and wordplay to present peanuts as a source of strength and to encourage motivation. It shows my ability to deliver a clear, engaging health message through persuasive visuals.

  2. 2
    2023Literature and MediaGroup project

    The Cask of Amontillado

    I created and designed the presentation analyzing Edgar Allan Poe’s story. Our work explored its characters, setting, irony and central themes of revenge, deceit and murder, and broke the plot into key stages from exposition to resolution. The project strengthened my skills in literary analysis, presentation design and teamwork.

    View presentation →
  3. 3
    2024Upskill ProgramCollaborative project

    Ahmed Helmy: career and values

    A presentation on the career of the Egyptian actor Ahmed Helmy and the values portrayed in his films. We examined selected movies, including their plots, characters and positive messages about self-development, relationships, ambition and humor. I contributed to both the research and the slide design.

    View presentation →
  4. 4
    2024Literature and CinemaGroup project

    Alice in Wonderland, book and film

    A presentation analyzing Lewis Carroll’s Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland and Tim Burton’s 2010 film adaptation. We compared plot, characters, themes and style, focusing on how Burton reimagined the whimsical story in a darker, more visual form. I designed the slides and contributed to the research and analysis.

    View presentation →
  5. 5
    2024Literature and SocietyResearch presentation

    The Running Man

    A research-based presentation on Stephen King’s novel and its themes of media control, social inequality and dehumanization in a dystopian world. I researched the historical and political context, analyzed the characters and tone, and designed the entire presentation.

    View presentation →
  6. 6
    2024Forensic LinguisticsSlides and audio

    Emergency Calls

    A presentation with an accompanying audio recording, analyzing a 911 call transcript to show how language works in real emergencies. I focused on dialogue structure, the caller’s emotional tone and the call taker’s responses, and on how pauses, repetition and voice changes can serve as evidence in investigations.

    View presentation →
  7. 7
    2024Language and GenderPresentation

    My Fair Lady through Lakoff

    A presentation applying Robin Lakoff’s feminist linguistic theory from Language and Woman’s Place to My Fair Lady. I analyzed key scenes and dialogue to show how language reflects gender roles, power dynamics and class distinctions.

    View presentation →
  8. 8
    2025Research Proposal, 1st termGroup research

    Breaking the Beauty Myth, Part 1

    Feminist theories on appearance, identity and mental health. The presentation summarized our group research proposal and explored how beauty standards affect women’s mental and physical health, with a film analysis of The Substance (2024). I designed the slides to present the thesis, aims and key theories clearly, from introduction to conclusion.

    View presentation →
  9. 9
    2025Research Proposal, 2nd termGroup research

    Breaking the Beauty Myth, Part 2

    The second part of the research project, applied to Toni Morrison’s The Bluest Eye. I designed the slides on how beauty standards, race and gender shape identity and mental health in the novel, covering Eurocentric beauty ideals, internalized norms and resistance through narrative.

    View presentation →
